Forbidden Love #2

Wildest Dreams

L.J. Shen, Maria Dosei (Translator)

4.16
35,549 ratings2,852 reviews
Rate this book
Cea mai profitabilă minciună din Manhattan are un singur defect: începe să pară adevărată.

Rhyland Coltridge este definiția gratificării instantanee. Un hedonist declarat și un strateg care a învățat de mult că imaginea valorează mai mult decât adevărul. Pentru el, Dylan Casablancas este singurul fruct cu adevărat oprit: sora mai mică a celui mai bun prieten, o mamă singură și o sursă constantă de iritare. Însă când un investitor îi confundă cu un cuplu solid, Rhyland vede o oportunitate. Are nevoie de o imagine de familist pentru a-și asigura contractul carierei lui, iar Dylan este singura care îi poate oferi această acoperire.

Dylan nu are timp pentru aroganța lui Rhyland. Viața ei în Manhattan este un haos: o fiică mică de crescut și un fost iubit toxic, care refuză să rămână în trecut. Rhyland este ultimul bărbat pe care l-ar accepta în preajmă, dar el îi oferă un târg pe care nu-l poate refuza: protecție totală în schimbul unei logodne false. Regulile sunt clare: fără sentimente, fără complicații, doar un contract temporar.

Însă sub luminile orașului, prefăcătoria începe să ardă. Între cinele oficiale și gesturile de tandrețe mimată, linia dintre jocul de scenă și dorință se șterge brutal. Rhyland a jurat că nu se va atinge de sora prietenului său, dar tentația este prea mare pentru un bărbat care nu știe să spună „nu”. Când contractul va fi semnat, Dylan va pleca. Dar marea problemă este că, după ce ai gustat dintr-un vis interzis, realitatea s-ar putea să nu mai fie niciodată suficientă.

Fairuz ᥫ᭡.
507 reviews1,651 followers
April 11, 2025
What is L.J. Shen’s obsession with dangling potential couples and then SWITCHING THEM UP last minute like it’s some kinda game show?! Like… HELLO??? First, we had Oliver and Frankie, but PLOT TWIST — Frankie gets benched and Briar takes her spot, and honestly?? That twist ate. So I was like fine, fine, I trust her. BUT THEN… DYLAN AND KIERAN??? JUST KIDDING, IT’S RHYLAND.

And to the agent who said “Where’s the tension in Kieran and Dylan?”
BE SO SERIOUS. Because this book had negative tension and a WHOLE lotta cringe. You gave us a setup and then threw it out like last season’s TikTok trend. I’m TIRED.

Now, onto the book… or whatever this fever dream was.

Let me start with Dylan. I don’t even know what to say. She's just kinda there, giving confused energy with a sprinkle of sass and a pinch of “why are you making these choices??”

But Rhyland? ABSOLUTELY NOT.

Like the first 50 pages were basically just him throwing degrading, obnoxious, sexist trash lines like it’s his job. Bro, if I wanted to read about a man constantly insulting a woman while imagining undressing her every 4.5 seconds, I’d go reread a Wattpad fic from 2013. Where is the growth? Where is the depth? WHERE IS THE BARE MINIMUM??

Also, I’m sorry but the POP CULTURE REFERENCES??? NO. NO NO NO. I can handle a lil Taylor Swift lyric here and there but NARA SMITH??? TikTok trends??? Bro Code??? SIX FIVE BLUE EYES??? It felt like the book was screaming "I’M HIP AND RELATABLE!” every three paragraphs. STOP. IT.

This was my 6th book by LJ Shen and it’s been a wild rollercoaster —
Hated 2
Liked 1
Mixed feelings about 2
And this one? It BROKE ME.

I swear the highlight of the entire book was Mr. Mushroom. And maybe Gravity, even though I still don’t like that name.

Some moments? Okay-ish. A tiny spark here and there. A few banter lines that didn’t make me want to DNF on the spot. But overall? A HOT MESS.

Tropes that were SUPPOSED to be there but flopped:
🌸 Enemies to lovers
💍 Fake engagement
🌸 Forbidden romance
💍 Best friend’s sister
🌸 Forced proximity
💍 Alpha hero
🌸 Single mom

But none of it HITS like it should. The tension? Flat. The spice? Meh. The emotions? Missing.

TL;DR:
It’s not me, it’s you.
No, actually — it IS you, Rhyland.

Dear L.J. Shen, I still love you, but this ain’t it. Please stop with the couple baiting. Please chill on the TikTok lingo. And PLEASE give us heroes that are love interests, not insults in human form.

He was pretty adamant in the beginning that he didn’t like kids, but Dylan’s daughter Gravity made him eat his words, he became a marshmallow of a man around her and it was so precious to read, these two were meant to be in each others lives in whatever capacity.

Dylan was a hot mess, raising her daughter by herself from scratch, working in a dead end job in a coffee shop until her brother came to the rescue and offered his place in New York on a silver platter.

These two were in and out of each others lives as young as six years old, which in turn grew into a small town crush on her brothers best friend, to outright enemies. Now living in the same apartment block was bound to make things interesting, and interesting it gets, he needs her help with nabbing a contract and standing in as his fake fiance, I had my doubts with this mutual arrangement because these two couldn't help cutting each other down when in each others orbit, the too and fro was like watching a tennis match, but in her times of need and no-one else she was able to lean on, Ryland became her pillar of strength.

The chemistry sizzled between these two, when the lines between hate and more became blurred was chefs kiss.

Dylan is trying to keep her ex at bay; Rhyland needs to land a deal worth millions. When the two form a fake engagement arrangement to achieve their goals, it seems all their problems are solved. But as they grow closer than their contract allows for, both will have to decide where the fake ends and the real begins.

Forbidden love is one of those tropes that seems to be a magnet for me. So needless to say, this brother’s best friend, forbidden love story was love at first sight. I mean, just look at this gorgeous cover! 😍 And yet, like the first book in the series, Shen turns a typically angsty trope on its head and makes it a whole lot of fun. From the steamy LOL beginning, straight through to the end, and all the swoony moments between our MCs in between, this was exactly the type of fun summer romance I was looking for.

⋆˚࿔ Review 𝜗𝜚˚⋆
3.5⭐️

Better than the first, but still not exactly a favorite.

First of all, Dylan. My girl. My comedic relief. She absolutely carried this book on her back like a pro. Every time she appeared, I perked up, her humor, her vibe, everything about her was just top tier. I could read an entire book just about her being chaotic and hilarious.

Now… him. I was judging the entire time 😔 I really can’t help it, man-whores exhaust me. I’ve read too many of them and at this point I’m just tired. He had some cute moments, sure, but he wasn’t giving book-boyfriend material, let’s be real.

Their chemistry was definitely there like, off the charts lusty 🔥 but that’s exactly the problem. It was lust, not love. They were hot together but emotionally? Not that deep. That’s why I couldn’t go higher than 3.5.

Also… this author and plot twists? A complicated relationship. She sets up so many opportunities for juicy, shocking, make-me-gasp moments… and then somehow picks the most random, unnecessary ones. Like ma’am, that’s what you decided to go with? 🙁 The plot twist in this book felt like it came from the garbage bin, so out of left field and honestly a little lazy. She had gold right there and picked sand.

The baby daddy though. A massive cunt. Like every time he appeared, my blood pressure spiked. Truly the most infuriating character.

Overall, I’d say this book was an improvement from the first, mostly because Dylan existed and the chemistry worked. But between the weird plot choices and my general dislike for man-whores, it didn’t completely win me over.

One thing I always look forward to with a L.J. Shen book is banter, and this had some absolutely amazing and hilarious banter. Dylan and Rhyland’s chemistry was off the charts. The way they were able to just bounce off of each other with the quick whips. They truly fit perfectly together.

I loved how Dylan was unapologetically herself. Her quick barbs and comebacks, and her love and adoration of her daughter made me like her even more. Along with her tenacity. Being a single mother, while rewarding in the form of her amazing daughter, isn’t easy, and Dylan showed that beautifully. All the highs and the lows.

Rhyland truly surprised me. I liked him in TMD, but I completely adored and loved him by the end of this. All the hidden layers of him that were peeled back has me down bad for this man.

Gravity was beyond adorable. I loved every scene she was in and the bright, innocent energy she brought. Her interactions with Rhyland were hilarious, wholesome, and so cute. The slow formation of their bond was everything.

Expect lots of laughter, some tears shed, some anger, fantastic banter as usual, and some spice that spices.

I received an advanced copy and this is my voluntary review.

I loved the way motherhood is portrayed in this story. It’s hard, and L.J. makes it clear how hard it is for a single mother. The love Dylan has for her daughter is absolutely heartwarming.. even more so when Rhy becomes a complete softy for her after claiming he wants nothing to do with children. It was easily one of my favorite parts of this story.. especially the “words of affirmation” scenes with Grav and Rhy.

The tension between Rhy & Dylan is piping hot and starts very early in the book and the slow burn is absolutely perfect.. because when they finally break the tension and give in.. it’s a 10/10. Rhy is a little freak and I LOVE IT!

2.5 unromantic ⭐️

I have a long history, of loving LJ Shen’s stories. I however did not love My dark Romeo (1⭐️) or Truly, madly, deeply (3⭐️) and unfortunately I am going for 3 for 3, with Wildest dreams.

The disappointment is real, and I was on the struggle bus with this one, I was actually driving the struggle bus to finish it.
It is long and kind of boring. What I have loved from LJ Shen’s previous books is the level of feels, I usually get, ups and downs and I am right there on the page with the characters.
The last few books has been shallow on the feelings end, and this book is removing her from my auto buy list. I am very sad about the downgrade.

Do publishers push authors to mass produce under time pressure? It could certainly feels like it as a reader.

The main characters are kind of shallow and the banter bordering on dumb. At chapter 20 I was still trying hard to be emotionally involved. This does get better, but not enough to have any feels.

I did have a little difficulty with Rhyland having been a male prostitute, and Dylan offering to sleep with him for money. That will have to be handled delicately, in order for me to love or even like them. But it’s like it’s just out there, and not even that important to the story. It’s too big of a deal for it not to be handled. It’s not worth it as a “shock effect “.

Dylan is rude most of the time, and I don’t really like her. She is making bad decisions and honestly she is not really a great mom. Gravity is taking up too much space in the story, and hence the romance is suffering. The friendships between Ro, Tate and Cal are all toxic under a disguise of friendships, and I did not fully understand the dynamics.

Honestly this isn’t a bad story but it’s not a good one either. It definitely is not a romance. More of a “the everyday life in a single mom.”

Angst: 0/10

Story 3/10

From the get-go I was hooked by Dylan — a single mum, keeping her guard up, trying to do right by her daughter while not waiting around for the hero-rescue. Then there’s Rhyland. He’s the classic “I don’t do relationships” type, wealthy, charming, bit messy — and watching him soften (especially around Dylan’s daughter) made me root for him harder than I expected.
The fake-engagement setup isn’t new, but it’s carried off with enough sharp banter, emotional undercurrents, and genuine stakes that it doesn’t feel flat. I laughed at their sass, I cringed at their mistakes, and I more than once paused and thought: “Oh wow, this might mean something real.” The daughter subplot? It’s sweet and adds a layer of heart that elevates the story beyond just two adults falling in love.
That said — the pace of them getting from “deal” to “real feelings” was slightly quicker than I’d have liked. At times I was ready for a bit more inner-process, more “why him now?” or “how did I get here?” moments. Also, the familiar tropes (single mom, billionaire playboy, fake fiancé) were used nicely, but if you’ve read a lot of similar stories you might see where the plot is headed early.

НО като изключим това, книгата е първата от мнооооооого време насам, която ме увлече и прочетох на един дъх без да усетя отегчение, досада, да въртя очи на малоумни сюжетни решения или да предизвиква позиви за повръщане заради претруфен изказ. Смях се като кретен, проблемите имаха основателен корен, мотивите зад поведението на героите бяха добре артикулирани и правдоподобни, самото то беше съответстващо на миналото им и последователно в стечение на историята. Диалозите бяха to die for, смъта беше OMFG hot, историята се лееше без проблеми. Хуморът и драмата бяха добре балансирани. Темите бяха релевантни и уважително представени. Дори хлапето не ме дразнеше, което за мен е цяло чудо. Имаше тук-там още едно-две неща, които бяха out of nowhere, но съм склонна да простя. Бели кахъри в сравнение с всичко останало хубаво, което се случваше в Wildest Dreams.
